request.system:
You are the test generator in Ledger. For one verified business rule of a legacy COBOL batch program you write test fixtures: complete, consistent sets of input records that exercise each branch of the rule and its boundaries. Every case is run through both the original COBOL program and a Python port, and their outputs are compared field by field, so a good case makes the rule's behaviour visible in the output files.

Guidance:
- One case per branch of the rule's When conditions, plus boundaries: values exactly at a limit, one cent over, a date equal to the limit and the day after, combinations of conditions where the rule says one result overrides another, zero and negative amounts where they matter.
- Keep each case small (normally 1-4 records per file) but complete: every file the program reads gets consistent records with matching keys, unless the case is deliberately about a missing record.
- Give values as strings: alphanumeric fields as text, numeric fields as plain decimal numbers such as "1250.75" or "-40.00" (no sign encoding, no padding). Omitted numeric fields default to 0 and omitted alphanumeric fields to spaces. Use the copybook field names exactly.
- Call check_fixture on each fixture before you submit it and fix every error. Warnings may be intentional (for example a card that is deliberately missing).
- Write 3 to 6 cases. In "expectation", say what the rule implies should happen; it is a note for reviewers, not the pass/fail oracle.

messages.content:
Program: CBACT04C. Input files and their record layouts:

TCATBAL: CVTRA01Y TRAN-CAT-BAL-RECORD (50 bytes)
  TRANCAT-ACCT-ID              9(11)
  TRANCAT-TYPE-CD              X(2)
  TRANCAT-CD                   9(4)
  TRAN-CAT-BAL                 S9(9)V9(2)

XREF: CVACT03Y CARD-XREF-RECORD (50 bytes)
  XREF-CARD-NUM                X(16)
  XREF-CUST-ID                 9(9)
  XREF-ACCT-ID                 9(11)

ACCOUNT: CVACT01Y ACCOUNT-RECORD (300 bytes)
  ACCT-ID                      9(11)
  ACCT-ACTIVE-STATUS           X(1)
  ACCT-CURR-BAL                S9(10)V9(2)
  ACCT-CREDIT-LIMIT            S9(10)V9(2)
  ACCT-CASH-CREDIT-LIMIT       S9(10)V9(2)
  ACCT-OPEN-DATE               X(10)
  ACCT-EXPIRAION-DATE          X(10)
  ACCT-REISSUE-DATE            X(10)
  ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT         S9(10)V9(2)
  ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT          S9(10)V9(2)
  ACCT-ADDR-ZIP                X(10)
  ACCT-GROUP-ID                X(10)

DISCGRP: CVTRA02Y DIS-GROUP-RECORD (50 bytes)
  DIS-ACCT-GROUP-ID            X(10)
  DIS-TRAN-TYPE-CD             X(2)
  DIS-TRAN-CAT-CD              9(4)
  DIS-INT-RATE                 S9(4)V9(2)
The program runs with job PARM '2022071800'. Account, cross-reference and disclosure group files are read by key, so every category balance's account needs ACCOUNT and XREF records.

Rule to test:
{
 "id": "BR-CBACT04C-002",
 "title": "Account balance update with accumulated interest at account break",
 "summary": "When an account group ends because the next record belongs to a different account, the account's interest total is added to its current balance, the current-cycle credit and debit are set to zero, and the account record is rewritten. Because of how the loop is written, the last account group in the file is never updated.",
 "given": [
  {
   "text": "Each calculated monthly interest amount is added to an interest total for the account. The total holds 9 integer digits and 2 decimals, signed.",
   "fields": [
    "WS-MONTHLY-INT",
    "WS-TOTAL-INT"
   ],
   "literals": []
  }
 ],
 "when": [
  {
   "text": "1050-UPDATE-ACCOUNT runs when a record for a new account arrives and it is not the first account group.",
   "fields": [
    "TRANCAT-ACCT-ID",
    "WS-LAST-ACCT-NUM",
    "WS-FIRST-TIME"
   ],
   "literals": [
    "Y"
   ]
  }
 ],
 "then": [
  {
   "text": "The account's interest total is added to its current balance (signed, 10 integer digits and 2 decimals).",
   "fields": [
    "WS-TOTAL-INT",
    "ACCT-CURR-BAL"
   ],
   "literals": []
  },
  {
   "text": "The account's current-cycle credit and current-cycle debit are both set to 0. This happens even when the interest total is zero.",
   "fields": [
    "ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT",
    "ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT"
   ],
   "literals": [
    "0"
   ]
  },
  {
   "text": "The updated account record overwrites the existing account record in the account file.",
   "fields": [
    "FD-ACCTFILE-REC",
    "ACCOUNT-RECORD"
   ],
   "literals": []
  },
  {
   "text": "When the read hits end of file, END-OF-FILE becomes 'Y' inside the iteration. The loop condition is tested before each pass, so the loop ends before the ELSE branch that would update the last account can run. The last account group's interest is therefore not added and that account record is not rewritten.",
   "fields": [
    "END-OF-FILE"
   ],
   "literals": [
    "Y",
    "N"
   ]
  }
 ]
}

condition.description: which branch or boundary of the rule this case exercises

expectation.description: what the rule says should happen (a note, not an oracle)

tools.description: Encode a fixture with the copybook layouts and check field names, PIC fit, key uniqueness and cross-file consistency.
